paper_title: MMRA A Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Granularity and Multi-Image   Relational Association Capabilities in Large Visual Language Models
caption: The number and ratio of each subtask in our MMRA benchmark. The integers in the graph represent the number of samples in each task, while the percentages in parentheses indicate the proportion of each task in the entire benchmark.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of sample counts and proportional representation across the ten subtasks that constitute the MMRA benchmark, designed to evaluate multi-granularity and multi-image relational association capabilities in large visual language models. Each slice corresponds to a distinct subtask, labeled with its name, sample count, and percentage of the total benchmark. The largest slice is “ObservationAngle” with 126 samples (12.28%), followed by “SimilarMaterial” with 106 (10.33%), and “SubEvent” with 100 (9.74%). Three subtasks — “SimilarEvent,” “AppearanceSimilarity,” and “Layout” — each contain 90 samples (8.77% each), while “Environment” also has 90 samples (8.77%). “MentalitySimilarity” accounts for 89 samples (8.67%), “RelativePosition” for 81 (7.90%), and the smallest slice, “NearSameEntity,” contains 63 samples (6.34%). The chart uses distinct colors for each category and includes both absolute counts and percentage values within each slice, enabling a clear visual comparison of task distribution across the benchmark.
